signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + RBA Shift
signals.text: AUD/CHF trades at 0.5704, with the G10 scorecard confirming CHF as the strongest peer (+0.925% 1W avg across 6 pairs) and AUD as the weakest (-0.792% across 4 pairs), generating a 1.717% leader-to-laggard spread. Despite the RBA raising its cash rate 25bps to 4.85% today (RBA 4.85% vs SNB 0.00% — +485bp carry advantage), Governor Bullock dropped explicit tightening guidance and stated uncertainty over future rate needs, sparking an AUD selloff. Meanwhile, Swiss headline CPI rose to 1.5% in October, reinforcing SNB stability while VIX sits elevated at 21.1. Technically, AUD/USD holds just above its SMA20 at 0.6997 but remains capped below its SMA50/200 cluster (0.7066/0.7060), offering no structural trend edge to counteract CHF momentum. Trade bias: Short AUD/CHF; dovish RBA re-pricing overrides AUD's carry advantage against safe-haven CHF demand. Catalyst: US ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI at 15:00 UTC. Risk: VIX drops back below 18, relieving cross-asset stress and re-establishing the 485bp carry floor.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Crowded Short + Option Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.852, hovering right above its SMA20 at 157.90 with the 200-day moving average capping upside at 158.48. OIS differentials maintain a massive carry advantage for the dollar (SOFR 3.95% vs TONA 1.23% — +272bp favors USD; Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%). Options markets display heavy downside demand, with 25d Risk Reversals printing an extreme -2.03 put skew (Saxo Bank, 1M tenor, indicative mid) while COT Leveraged Funds remain net short JPY at -19,224 contracts (94th percentile of its 52w range, z=+1.57). With VIX elevated at 21.1, the high 272bp carry spread continues to hold spot, but extreme options put skew indicates institutions are aggressively hedging against a sudden unwind toward 160.00 intervention watch levels. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry advantage sustains spot above moving averages despite option tail-risk hedging. Catalyst: US JOLTS Job Openings and ISM Services PMI at 15:00 UTC. Risk: A sustained VIX surge past 25 triggers a forced carry liquidation, breaking spot below SMA20 at 157.90.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Retail Extreme + ESI Drag
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5629, pinned below its SMA20 (0.5642) and SMA50 (0.5724) within a tight 20-session range box. Retail sentiment on Retail sentiment data shows an extreme 85% long / 15% short bias, creating a severe contrarian reversal risk as retail traders attempt to catch a falling knife. Fundamental backing remains weak, as New Zealand's Economic Surprise Index sits at a strong negative -18.1 with persistent macro data misses, while COT positioning shows Leveraged Funds net short -22,722 contracts. Although the Fed (4.00%) vs RBNZ (2.75%) policy spread yields a 125bp carry advantage to the dollar, retail remains stubborn despite negative momentum. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD; retail extreme long positioning faces ongoing unwind pressure into weak macro fundamentals. Catalyst: New Zealand Employment Change at 21:45 UTC. Risk: Strong NZ employment data beats consensus expectations (+0.4% q/q), triggering a short-covering rally back toward 0.5700.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Rates Split + Volatility Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD sits at 1.1202, maintaining a counter-trend pullback posture below its SMA20 (1.1200) and SMA50 (1.1382). US 5Y yield decomposition shows nominal yields falling 31bp over 20D (FRED, as of Oct 29) split between real yields (-42bp) and breakevens (+11bp) — a real-yield-led decline that moderates broad USD momentum. However, OIS benchmarks confirm a 151bp carry premium in favor of the dollar (SOFR 3.95% vs €STR 2.44%; Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65%). 1M ATM Implied Volatility for EUR/USD sits at 6.0% against 30-day Realized Volatility of 4.4% (Saxo Bank FX Options Analytics), yielding a +1.6% Vol Risk Premium as options markets price election and geopolitical headline protection ahead of key US economic releases. Trade bias: Range/Neutral EUR/USD; falling US real yields offset Eurozone macro weakness and dollar carry dominance. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI YoY at 10:00 UTC followed by US ADP/ISM data. Risk: Euro Area CPI misses expectations (<3.4%), widening the rate differential expectation and forcing spot below 1.1180.

signals.title: USD/CAD — COT Short vs Yield Spread Compression
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.3963, dropping below its SMA20 (1.4110) and SMA50 (1.4030) as short-term technical structure shows reversal risk against the preceding uptrend. OIS rates show for the greenback (SOFR 3.95% vs CORRA 2.55%; Fed 4.00% vs BoC 2.25%), but 2Y yield spreads have narrowed by +28bp in CAD's favor over the last 5 sessions to -129bp. CFTC COT data highlights CAD Leveraged Funds at a net short position of -96,952 contracts (pctl 8, z=-1.55), indicating stretched institutional short positioning that leaves the pair vulnerable to mean-reversion squeezes if Canadian data continues to stabilize. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD; technical breakdown below key moving averages supported by 2Y yield momentum and crowded CAD spec shorts. Catalyst: US & Canada Trade Balance releases at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Crude oil prices reverse intraday gains (+1.30% WTI at $97.7), reopening downside risks for the Canadian dollar back above 1.4030.
